about: Workout library for the X Millas 2027 block. Hand-maintained (like plan.json). plan.json key sessions reference these by id. Evidence: strong = trials/large cohorts; moderate = small studies; consensus = coaching practice, little direct research; your-data = from your own past X Millas editions.

course_facts.mid_climb: Mid-race climb: 1.75 km at 4.3% (+76 m), mile 3.5–4.6. PB 10:00.
course_facts.finish_drag: Finish drag: 3.15 km at 2.2% (+71 m), mile 7.8–9.8. PB 16:18.
course_facts.fade: In non-PB years the finish drag cost 3.5–6% more grade-adjusted effort than the mid-race climb. In the 2023 PB they were level.

workouts.name: Easy run
workouts.what: Conversational running, nose-breathing pace, flat or rolling.
workouts.why: Builds the aerobic base (capillaries, mitochondria, fat use) and, more importantly here, lets bone, tendon and calf tissue adapt to road impact at a load they can absorb.
workouts.for_xmillas: Most of the block's distance. Road running is harsher than the hiking-heavy GTCB build, so this is where the tissue catches up.
workouts.how: Truly easy. If in doubt, slower. Walk a hill rather than grind it.
workouts.watch_out: Easy days drifting into steady. That steals recovery from the key sessions.

workouts.name: Strides (flat)
workouts.what: 4–8 × ~20 s smooth accelerations to about mile-race pace, full walk/jog recovery.
workouts.why: Keeps leg speed and running form sharp at almost no fatigue cost. Reminds the nervous system how to run fast and relaxed.
workouts.for_xmillas: Re-finds turnover after months of ultra pace and hiking. It also primes the quick, relaxed descents where 2026 lost the most time.
workouts.how: After an easy run. Build up, hold for a few seconds, float down. Never sprint flat out.
workouts.watch_out: Cold, tight calves: do them at the end of the run, not the start.

workouts.name: Hill strides
workouts.what: 6–10 × ~20 s brisk running up a 4–8% hill, walk down.
workouts.why: Recruits more muscle fibre and builds uphill power. The hill limits speed and impact, so you get a strong stimulus with less hamstring and impact risk than flat sprinting.
workouts.for_xmillas: First uphill stimulus of the block: power without fatigue, before any rep that could cause a fade.
workouts.how: Tall posture, quick short steps, drive the arms. Stop each one before form breaks. Walk all the way down.
workouts.watch_out: Calf load is high going uphill on the forefoot. Keep reps short and stop if the calf talks.

workouts.name: Calf raises
workouts.what: Single-leg raises, straight knee (gastrocnemius) and bent knee (soleus), slow lowering.
workouts.why: The calf, especially the soleus, takes several times body weight with every running step. Strength gives it margin, and climbing loads it hardest.
workouts.for_xmillas: Calf trouble was behind the 2024 run/walk race. It's the precaution watch on the dashboard, and every hill session leans on it.
workouts.how: 2–3×/wk, 3 × 10–15 per leg each type, 3 s lowering. Add a backpack load once 15 is easy.
workouts.watch_out: Do them after runs or on rest days, not right before hill work.

workouts.name: Long run
workouts.what: The week's longest run, easy effort, rolling terrain later in the block.
workouts.why: Builds durability: running economy holds up better late in a run when long runs are regular. Also the big tissue-loading session of the week.
workouts.for_xmillas: Durability is the late-race fade. The finish drag starts after 12.6 km, and the long run is how 12.6 km stops feeling long.
workouts.how: Grow it gently. Keep each long run within about 10% of your longest run in the last 30 days. The dashboard flags a spike.
workouts.watch_out: A large cohort study (5,200 runners) found injury risk rose when one run was >10% longer than the 30-day longest. Weekly-total rules showed no such link.

sources.label: Frandsen, Nielsen et al. 2025, BJSM — single-session spikes

workouts.name: Benchmark climb
workouts.what: Same local road climb (3–5%, 3–6 min), same effort, every recovery week.
workouts.why: A repeatable test that shows if uphill running is getting stronger: faster at the same heart rate, or the same time at a lower one.
workouts.for_xmillas: The direct measure of the block's main target, retested in W4, W8, W12 and W16.
workouts.how: Warm up 15 min. Run it at controlled hard effort, like the mid-race climb, not flat out. Note time, avg HR, how it felt.
workouts.watch_out: Weather, wind and fatigue skew it. Compare HR and time together, and do it fresh.

workouts.name: Short hill reps
workouts.what: 8–10 × 45 s or 6 × 90 s up 4–8%, at about 5 km effort. Jog down.
workouts.why: Uphill intervals improve running economy and 5 km performance. In a 6-week trial, the hardest uphill program gave the clearest economy gain (~2.4%).
workouts.for_xmillas: Builds the uphill engine and the strength to hold form on the steep parts of the mid-race climb (sections up to 8–10%).
workouts.how: Strong but controlled. The last rep should match the first. Full jog-down recovery.
workouts.watch_out: Racing the reps. If pace drops >5% across the set, stop: that's the fade you're training out, not into.

sources.label: Barnes et al. 2013, IJSPP — uphill interval programs

workouts.name: Steady / tempo
workouts.what: 15–20 min continuous at comfortably hard: about half-marathon effort, a few words at a time.
workouts.why: Raises the pace you can hold without lactate climbing. A 10-miler is run just under this threshold.
workouts.for_xmillas: Race effort for 16 km is just under threshold. This is the flat half of the race-pace engine.
workouts.how: Even effort, not even pace, on rolling ground. Finish feeling you could do 5 more min.

workouts.name: Long hill reps
workouts.what: 5–6 × 3–4 min up 3–5% at race effort, jog down.
workouts.why: Longer reps train the ability to sustain uphill effort, not just produce it. Same family as the uphill intervals research.
workouts.for_xmillas: Mid-race climb sim: 1.75 km at 4.3% took 10 min in the PB. 3–4 min reps at that grade rehearse it in chunks.
workouts.how: Race effort, by feel and HR, not pace. Hold posture and cadence to the top of each rep.
workouts.watch_out: Effort creep on later reps. The goal is even reps.

workouts.name: Climb tempo
workouts.what: 2 × 8 min (building to 12 min) continuous up a long gentle 2–3% drag at tempo effort.
workouts.why: Trains steady threshold-type effort on a shallow climb: the hardest kind of uphill to pace, because it's runnable all the way.
workouts.for_xmillas: Finish-drag sim: 3.15 km at 2.2% took 16:18 in the PB. This is where the fade has shown up every non-PB year.
workouts.how: Find a long gentle road drag. Hold effort, not pace, and run tall. Shorten the stride rather than slow the cadence.
workouts.watch_out: Starting too hard. The drag punishes the first minute's ego for the last five.

workouts.name: Climbing on tired legs
workouts.what: Steady running first (30 min or a long run), then a sustained climb at effort.
workouts.why: Running economy, including uphill, worsens as fatigue builds. Practising climbing after running trains the durability to hold it.
workouts.for_xmillas: THE target. Your data: climbs are fine fresh, but the late climb costs 3.5–6% more effort. This session rehearses exactly that.
workouts.how: Easy-to-steady first part, then the climb at controlled race effort. Judge it by the last minute: still running tall?
workouts.watch_out: It's a double load. Never in the same week as a long-run spike, and skip it if the calf flags.

sources.label: Changes in running economy during a 65-km ultra (uphill economy worsens with fatigue)

workouts.name: Course simulation
workouts.what: About 10 km rolling at steady effort straight into ~3 km of climbing at race effort.
workouts.why: Rehearses the race's shape (descents, rollers, then the long climb) so pacing and fuelling are known before race day.
workouts.for_xmillas: Mirrors km 0–12.6 into the finish drag. If you're in Alfàs, run the real course.
workouts.how: Hold back early, as on race day. Descents relaxed and quick, then commit on the climb.
workouts.watch_out: The biggest single session of the block. Treat the next 2 days as easy.

workouts.name: Race-effort hill miles
workouts.what: 3 × 1 mile at race effort, each including a climb, 3 min jog between.
workouts.why: Sharpens the feel of race effort over mixed terrain without the cost of a full simulation.
workouts.for_xmillas: Locks in the effort you want on the mid-race climb and the finish drag, by feel.
workouts.how: Even effort across each mile: let pace drop on the climb and recover on the flat.
workouts.watch_out: Too fast in taper season. You can't gain fitness now, only lose freshness.

workouts.name: Downhill strides
workouts.what: 6 × 20 s quick, relaxed running down a gentle 3–5% slope, walk back up.
workouts.why: Downhill running builds eccentric quad tolerance (the 'repeated bout effect'). Earlier bouts reduce soreness and fatigue from later ones.
workouts.for_xmillas: 2026's biggest loss vs the PB was the first descent (+165 s). Quick, relaxed descending is free time.
workouts.how: Lean slightly forward, quick light steps, arms loose. Gentle grade only.
workouts.watch_out: Steep grades and long reps hammer the quads and knees. Keep it short and gentle.

sources.label: Bontemps et al. 2024, EJSS — repeated downhill bouts

workouts.name: Shakeout
workouts.what: 20–30 min very easy plus a few strides.
workouts.why: Keeps the legs moving and sharp without adding load.
workouts.for_xmillas: Race week: arrive fresh, not flat.
workouts.how: Short and easy. A few strides at the end.

workouts.name: X Millas
workouts.what: 10 mi, l'Alfàs del Pi, Sun 18 Apr 2027.
workouts.for_xmillas: Plan: hold back on the first descent but run it quick and relaxed. Even effort up the mid-race climb. Save something for the finish drag and hold effort to the top.
workouts.how: Effort, not pace. The finish drag is where the race is decided.
workouts.watch_out: Heat: 4 of 5 editions were hot. Hydrate the day before (the 2023 lesson).
